contract: Each side opens the same preloaded seekable file, reads every packet, folds the stream index and its published additions, and tears the reader down.
Kind 4 subtypes are opaque BlockAdditional wire bytes (including the 8-byte big-endian ID), LCEVC NAL bytes and HDR10+ fields, in that order.
HDR10+ rows contain application version, window count, targeted display luminance, targeted and mastering grids, and each window in order.

A grid contributes presence, dimensions and row-major samples over 15. A window contributes geometry presence, corners over 1 and ellipse fields when present, MaxSCL and average over 100000, then count and ordered percentile pairs, and bright-pixel fraction over 1000.
Tone-curve presence precedes both knee coordinates over 4095 and counted anchors over 1023. Saturation presence precedes weight over 8. Rationals fold numerator and denominator in that order.
Triergon derives the side data from each typed packet and checks the HDR result against the direct T.35 entry point. A terminal row distinguishes EOF from an input refusal.

open_deviations.reading: An HDR10+ message the BlockAdditional ends inside
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 section 5.1.3.5.2 with BlockAddIDType 4 (section 5.1.4.1.17): the BlockAdditional carries an ITU-T T.35 HDR10+ message, here cut after 13 bytes, before its syntax ends
open_deviations.candidate: returns the packets before it and the affected packet, then refuses with the truncated HDR10+ syntax
open_deviations.reference: returns the packets before it and reports the end of the stream without the affected packet

open_deviations.reading: Two BlockMore elements with the same effective BlockAddID
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 section 5.1.3.5.2.3: each BlockAddID MUST be unique among the BlockMore elements of a BlockAdditions element, and an omitted BlockAddID is 1
open_deviations.candidate: returns the first packet, then refuses the BlockAdditions that repeats BlockAddID 1
open_deviations.reference: keeps the last opaque addition and attaches it, with the LCEVC data, to both laces

open_deviations.reading: BlockAddID values above the track maximum
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 section 5.1.4.1.16: MaxBlockAdditionID is the maximum value of BlockAddID for the track
open_deviations.candidate: admits only WebM VP9's implicit ITU-T T.35 BlockAddID 4, then refuses the undeclared BlockAddID above the maximum
open_deviations.reference: exports the undeclared BlockAddIDs 2, 3 and 8, ignoring the maximum, and ends normally
open_deviations.compat: a consumer that needs additions above the maximum exported would use a compat::block_additions policy that admits them (not built)
